text:
kai: Hey team — ran an nsys trace of the low-latency path, seeing big memcpy bursts that look to block kernels on stream 0. timeline attached, but tl;dr: cudaMemcpyAsync spikes concurrent with small kernel launches. :thinking:
ashley: Can you paste the top 10 timeline hotpots? even a quick grep of kernel names helps.
kai: quick paste from nsys summary:
```
# top kernels by total time
kernel_attention_fwd  42.3ms
lm_kv_get            18.7ms
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D  31.2ms
triton::compute      25.4ms
kv_prefetch          9.6ms
```
mike: those cudaMemcpyAsync H2D spikes are suspicious — are we bouncing pinned vs pageable buffers? if pageable, driver syncs and stalls default stream.
ashley: IIRC our KV cache prefetch uses cudaMalloc + cudaMemcpy for new keys on demand (host-side memcpys). that could be forcing implicit syncs with default stream.
jonathan: try reproducing with nvprof/nsys using only the low-latency batch (batch_size=1) + --capture-range=cpu so we see host thread scheduling. I bet we have CPU scheduling gaps that align with memcpy syscalls.
perf-bot: perf summary (sampling):
- syscalls (memcpy): 12.4% cpu
- context-switches increased at 12:34:11.
- wakeups correlated with kv_prefetch thread.

kai: here's a short timeline observation: stream 1 runs kernels but stream 0 memcpy shows as long contiguous block, kernels only run after the big memcpy finishes — looks like either pinned/pageable issue or default-stream implicit sync.
mike: can you check whether those memcpys are using cudaMemcpyAsync with a non-zero stream and pinned host buffers? if they're not pinned, driver will sync. also check if code uses cudaDeviceSynchronize somewhere near prefetch.
ashley: we do call cudaHostAlloc for pinned buffers in the new prefetcher, but older code path still uses std::vector + memcpy -> cudaMemcpy (host pointer pageable). Maybe a mixed mode where some keys use pinned and others not.
jonathan: Another angle: kernel selection. small kernels (kv_get, small attention fragments) have high launch overhead. lots of tiny launches + memcpys cause serialization. batching heuristics might be creating many tiny invocations — maybe change to fuse small ops or increase batch window.
kai: Good call. Also noticed that when we force stream priorities (high-prio for inference kernels, low-prio for prefetch memcpys) overlap improves. but testing showed kernels still blocked until memcpy completes on same CUDA engine.
mike: stream priorities only help if operations are on different engines (copy engine vs compute). cudaMemcpyAsync between host-device uses copy engine; if the copy is synchronous due to pageable buffers, it will block compute. So pinned buffers fix it.
jonathan: For experiments: capture with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,cublas --sample=cpu --trace-fork-before-exec true` and run a workload with 50 short inferences. Then grep for `cudaMemcpy` events and check args for "HostPinned" vs not.
ashley: I'll schedule an s-replay job for the trace now. will include two branches: pinned-prefetch vs old-prefetch.
s-replay-bot: scheduled replay 1769904340 on perf-cluster-2, will upload nsys artifacts to /tmp/nsys/1769904340.zip when done. :white_check_mark:
kai: If pinned prefetch reduces memcpy blocking but we still see kernel launch overhead, we should try batching heuristics: 1) coalesce consecutive kv_gets into single kernel, 2) micro-batching window of 5ms, 3) fuse attention sub-kernels.
mike: Also consider enabling cuBLAS/CUBLASLt fused matmul kernels for small GEMMs — improves throughput and reduces kernel count.
jonathan: One more: check for CPU-side lock contention in our KV thread — if the prefetch thread holds a mutex while issuing cudaMemcpy calls, that can delay issuing kernels from main thread. use `perf lock` or instrument the mutex.
ashley: I'll capture a second nsys with `--capture-range=cpu` and attach perf lock output.
kai: Thanks — next steps: ashley runs pinned vs pageable trace, jonathan looks at perf lock traces, mike experiments with fused kernels, I'll analyze nsys timelines for stream overlap metrics. keep posts short, attach snippets where possible. :eyes:
